subject: Northshore Bank RFP - Failover commitments and evidence pack
messages:
From: Danielle Moore <d.moore@northshorebank.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Northshore Procurement <procurement@northshorebank.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Northshore RFP - DR & resilience clarifications

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet. The procurement and resilience teams had a few follow-up questions specifically around multi-region failover behavior and recovery objectives so we can finalize our risk scoring. Please confirm the items below and attach any runbook extracts or evidence we can include with our submission: 

1) For the hosted Redwood API, what is the typical automated failover RTO for a regional outage (triggered by health checks) assuming customer is on the hosted tier?
2) What RPO should we expect for ephemeral inference state versus customer-managed persistent artifacts (logs/metrics)?
3) Can you confirm how session affinity (for chat state) is preserved or reconstructed across regions?
4) Do you provide a warm-standby cross-region cluster option and what are the capacity commitments (e.g., % of production QPS reserved)?
5) Any compliance evidence (runbook excerpts, post-mortem examples, SOC2 artifact references) you can share that demonstrates past exercises or failovers?

We're on a tight review cadence and would appreciate a consolidated response by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Danielle
VP, Vendor Risk Management
Northshore Bank

--
Danielle Moore
Northshore Bank
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Moore <d.moore@northshorebank.com>
Cc: Northshore Procurement <procurement@northshorebank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Northshore RFP - DR & resilience clarifications

Hi Danielle — thank you for the clear list. We can provide a consolidated technical statement plus a short runbook extract and a warm-standby diagram. High-level answers below; see attached packet for operational detail and extracts. We'll also loop Karthik (solutions) and Lauren (sales) on a quick call if you'd like step-through.

Summary (hosted Redwood API):
- Automated regional failover (health-check triggered): typical RTO 15–60 minutes for API availability to the application layer with our default cross-region routing and degraded-capacity fallbacks.
- RPO: Ephemeral inference state is effectively stateless for most flows (chat KV caches are kept in an actively replicated cache with RPO < 60s when configured). Customer-managed persistent artifacts (logs, metrics, customer payloads) depend on retention config — default pipeline replicates telemetry to a durable store with near-real-time replication (RPO typically < 5 minutes).
- Session affinity and chat state: We use a tiered approach — short-lived KV cache (fast path) + persistent session metadata in the customer-scoped datastore. On failover we attempt KV reconstruction from prefix caches; if unavailable we fall back to the most recent persisted metadata and rerun a lightweight reconciliation. Typical observed user-visible session continuity varies with workload but most customers experience no more than a single failed token generation followed by resume behavior.
- Warm-standby option: yes — Redwood Dedicated/Warm mode reserves customer-configurable standby capacity. Typical commitment options: 25%, 50%, 100% of baseline QPS. 25% is common for cost-conscious bank use-cases. Standby instances are kept warmed (model weights loaded) and health-checked; promotion is automated with traffic shift controlled by Canary / circuit-breaker policies.
- Evidence: attached runbook extract (failure detection, escalation matrix, manual rollback steps), a redacted post-mortem timeline from a prior cross-region incident, and references to our SOC 2 Type II controls for change management and incident response (we can provide SOC report under NDA).

Attachments in this message: northshore_DR_response_packet.pdf (contains the runbook extract, architecture diagram, and redacted post-mortem).

If you'd like, we can provide a short 30-minute walkthrough with operations on Thursday at 10am ET to walk the runbook.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Northshore RFP - confirmation notes

Priya / Lauren — forwarding Danielle's questions and Priya's draft responses (attached). A couple of internal clarifications for the packet before we finalize: 

- The RTO band 15–60 minutes: make sure we explicitly call out conditions (full regional platform outage vs. degradations that are resolved by traffic routing). For SLA wording we should avoid hard guarantees on hosted tiers; offer SLA only for Dedicated customers.
- RPO language: quantify the cache TTL and replication interval in the packet (we currently replicate KV snapshots every 30s by default; add note that customers can tune to stricter intervals with traffic/IO trade-offs).
- Warm-standby commitments: include example cost delta for 25%/50%/100% reserves and how burst capacity works.

I'll draft the short addendum and update the PDF. Priya — do you want me to include a redacted timeline from the 2027 cross-region test exercise? That would help procurement.

-Karthik
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Northshore RFP - confirmation notes

Yes please — include the redacted 2027 test exercise timeline (ops drills are persuasive). Lauren — please prepare a short pricing addendum showing monthly delta for each standby % option against the proposed committed throughput. I'll attach both to the final packet and send to Danielle.

Also, Danielle — (cc'd) we can deliver the final consolidated packet with the addendum and redacted timeline by tomorrow EOD. Would you prefer the walkthrough before or after you review the final materials?

Thanks,
Priya
From: Danielle Moore <d.moore@northshorebank.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Northshore Procurement <procurement@northshorebank.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Northshore RFP - DR & resilience clarifications

Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the packet. The addendum and the redacted drill timeline answered most of our internal questions. Procurement would still like the explicit wording we discussed in the RFP appendix: a short paragraph describing the expected failover sequence (detection -> traffic reroute -> warm-standby promotion -> verification checks) and a line that clarifies SLA applicability (hosted vs dedicated). If you can put that into a concise Appendix A and share the link to the Drive folder, we can close this section of the RFP. A 30-minute ops walkthrough after we review the Appendix would be helpful.

Appreciate the collaboration — Danielle
VP, Vendor Risk Management
Northshore Bank
